RAJYA  SABHA

List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the August 23, 2007/Bhadrapada 1, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and
Urban Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs;

Total number of questions — 20
51
Misappropriation of funds by NGOs
*161. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the specific reasons for which large
number of NGOs, etc. have not submitted
utilization certificates vide Ministry's
Annual Report for the year 2006-07;
(b) whether any special efforts have
been made to recover the amount running
into hundreds of crores remaining un-
accounted for years;
(c) whether Government have
considered to file criminal cases against
the defaulting parties for breach of trust
and misappropriation of Government
funds;
(d) whether the involvement of
Ministry's officials in financial bungling has
been investigated; and
(e) if so, the results thereof?
Floors allowed under Master Plan
2021
*162. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI :
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of floors (excluding
Ground Floor) which have been allowed in
the Master Plan 2021 in the houses
constructed before 1st January, 2007;
(b) if those houses have any additional
floors, whether Government are considering
to regularize those floors by accepting
penalty charges; and
(c) whether Government are also
considering regularization of Hanging
Projections of those houses by charging
penalty amount?

52
Unwanted telemarketing calls
*163. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether TRAI has put in place
norms to ensure that telemarketeers do not
disturb phone users;
(b) to what extent the National Do Not
Call (NDNC) Registry would help poorer
sections to get access to it and ensure that
they are not disturbed;
(c) whether it is a fact that poorer
people would not be able to properly avail
of the ‘National Registry’;
(d) the steps proposed to evolve a
Registry with a positive list of subscribers
who welcome telemarketing; and
(e) the steps to protect people from
unwanted SMS messages?
Construction of houses under
JNNURM
*164. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre has sanctioned
Rs. 361 crores to Rajasthan under the
JNNURM for construction of 20,000 new
houses to replace the slums in seven towns
in the State;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are aware that
Orissa is among the most backward and
poverty-stricken region;
(d) if so, whether such a project is also
proposed to be sanctioned for Orissa State
to replace the slums; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Discontinuation of subsidy for Haj
pilgrimage
*165. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to discontinue the financial
subsidies to Haj pilgrims as per Allahabad
High Court Verdict; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Visit of relatives of PoWs in Pakistan
*166. SHRIMATI  JAYA
BACHCHAN:
SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a delegation
of kith and kins of 1971 war prisoners,
reportedly lodged in Pakistani jails visited
Pakistan recently on an invitation extended
by Government of Pakistan;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that on reaching
Pakistan, they were not allowed to visit
the jails;
(d) whether Government took up the
matter with the Government of Pakistan; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Drop in mobile phone signals
*167. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that locations
close to cantonments, defence areas and
airports report signal drops in mobile
phones;

53
(b) if so, whether TRAI has issued some
guidelines for giving relaxation to the
companies; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Cases received by CIC
*168. DR. CHANDAN MITRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the total number of cases (appeals/
complaints) received by the Central
Information Commission (CIC);
(b) the total number of cases in which
reviews have been filed;
(c) the number of cases in which non-
compliance with CIC orders has been
reported;
(d) the number of cases in which delay
in providing information has been reported
and out of these in how many cases, show
cause notice for imposition of penalty has
been issued and financial penalties were
finally imposed;
(e) the number of cases in which
financial penalty was withdrawn after
having been imposed; and
(f) the number of cases that have been
disposed of without holding any hearing?
Help to Indians in Oman
*169. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT :
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a high
velocity tornado played havoc with life and
property in Oman during the first week of
June, 2007;
(b) if so, the details of the losses
suffered by Indians living in Oman; and
(c) the help provided by Indian Mission
in Oman to Indians there to mitigate their
hardships?
Central schemes and Centrally
sponsored schemes
*170. SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the difference between Central
schemes and Centrally sponsored schemes;
(b) the number of schemes under each
of the two categories;
(c) the institutional mechanism to
implement such schemes;
(d) the modes of financial delegation and
financial sharing with the States under the
above two categories; and
(e) the monitoring and evaluation
mechanism for Central schemes and
Centrally sponsored schemes,
respectively?
Threat posed by climatic changes
*171. SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO
JOSHI: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of the
serious threat posed by the current climatic
changes like extremes of temperatures and
skewed distribution of rainfall, etc.; and
(b) whether any study is being carried
out to estimate the consequence for tropical
countries, particularly India and the
measures required to ensure food security
and sufficiency in foodgrains, dairy, fruits
and vegetables?

54
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
High acid content in rainwater
*172. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a study
conducted by the Indian Meteorological
Department (IMD) has found high acid
content in rainwater in Pune and Nagpur;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?
Celebration of Gandhi Jayanti
*173. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any plan for Indian
Missions to celebrate Gandhi Jayanti in a
special manner in view of the United
Nations declaring Gandhi Jayanti as
International Day of Non-violence; and
(b) whether there is any proposal to
involve friends interested in Mahatma
Gandhi in every country on that day?
Registration of case by CBI for
re-routing international
calls as local calls
*174. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
SHRI VIRENDRA BHATIA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that CBI had
registered a case against the officials of
erstwhile Reliance Infocom in September
2006 regarding rerouting of international
calls as local, which caused extensive loss
of revenue to Government; and
(b) the status of the case?
Population living on borders
†*175. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that China in an
agreement had agreed two years ago that
both the countries would protect the
interests of their population settled in the
border areas while sorting out the solution
of border dispute;
(b) whether it is also a fact that China is
now backing out of its said promise; and
(c) if so, Government's reaction thereto
and the steps being taken by Government
in this direction?
Takeover of Singareni Collieries
*176. SHRIMATI. N.P. DURGA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has proposed to takeover Singareni
Collieries as part of its move to form
National Coal Grid;
(b) whether any help or cooperation is
sought from the foreign companies or
institutions in the formation of National
Coal Grid;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the share of the Centre in the
Singareni Collieries?

55
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Non-performing contractors
*177. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that National
Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has
black-listed more than 20 domestic and
foreign companies and put them in "non-
performing" list for dragging Golden
Quadrilateral Highways projects;
(b) if so, the names of such firms and
the projects delayed by each of them;
(c) whether Government are also
considering imposing penalty on non-
performing contractors; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Impact of large dams on global
warming
*178. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the
recently published study by the scientists,
large dams in India are responsible for about
a fifth of the country's global warming
impact and Indian dams are the largest global
warming contributors compared to other
nations;
(b) whether it is a fact that the total
methane emissions from India's large dams
could be 33.5 million tonnes per annum; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to investigate this matter and the
action proposed?
Targets under Bharat Nirman Yojana
†*179. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) to what extent the 'Bharat Nirman
Yojana' of Government has achieved its
targets;
(b) whether any Committee has been
constituted for inquiry of its development;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Development of sports infrastructure
in NER
*180. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the names of those States, towns
and villages in North Eastern Region
especially in Assam where sports
infrastructure has been developed during
the last three years, district-wise/town-
wise/village-wise; and
(b) the effective steps taken or
proposed to be taken by Government for
development of sports infrastructure in all
the said States of NER?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,

278
Indo-Russian Nuclear Power
Collaboration
1209. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that with a fresh
impetus to Indo-Russian nuclear power
collaboration Russia has agreed to build up
10 nuclear units across various sites in India;
(b) whether Russia has already agreed
to four additional units at Koodankulam
Atomic Station while six more units could
be on the anvil across more sites;
(c) whether over 100 Russian firms are
already involved in the setting up of two
under construction 1,000 MW units in
Koodankulam;
(d) if so, whether these projects would
be funded by India; and
(e) by when they would be
completed?
 India's joining of ITER project
1210. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has
joined the International Thermo-nuclear
Experimental Reactor (ITER) project;
(b) if so, the details about Government's
fiscal involvement in this project;
(c) whether Government have planned
to constitute any authoritative board for
the effective implementation of this
project;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Nuclear Power Projects
1211. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to start two nuclear power
projects in Gujarat and Rajasthan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have plans to

279
start similar projects in Bihar and
Maharashtra; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Mining of titanium in Kerala
1212. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is large
deposit of titanium in the coastal Kerala,
fit for commercial exploitation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether a U.S. aircraft manufacturer
had evinced interest in mining the titanium
ore for making alloys used in the
manufacture of aircrafts, which the State
Government did not approve;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Russia has proposed to take
up exploitation of titanium in Kerala; and
(f) if so, the Centre's response thereto?
 Creation of a SPV
1213. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that select PSUs
are creating a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)
to acquire coal mines abroad;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for such a step; and
(d) the countries which have been
identified for such acquisitions?
 Non-utilisation of coal blocks
1214. SHRI EKANATH K.THAKUR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a
Parliamentary Committee has criticized the
Ministry of Coal for failing to ensure
development of captive coal blocks allotted
as back as 1998;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
lackadaisical approach of his Ministry in
monitoring the progress of captive coal
blocks allotted to different parties has
resulted in non-utilization of coal blocks
for exploration of coal; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to develop the coal blocks?
 Coal-mine accidents
1215. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of coal-mine accidents
that occurred in India during the last five
years, year-wise;
(b) the number of persons died in those
accidents;
(c) whether court of enquiry was set in
each case of accidents;
(d) if so, the major findings thereof; and
(e) the number of persons who have
been punished so far for the negligence
attributed to those accidents?
 Review of royalty on coal
†1216. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether some coal producing States
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

280
have sought to increase royalty of States
on coal;
(b) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard;
(c) whether the royalty given to the
States on coal is reviewed after every three
years under the Mines and Mineral
Development Regulatory Act; and
(d) if so, how many times such review
has been made so far and the results
thereof?
 Target fixed for various units of CIL
†1217. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the production target fixed for
various subsidiary units of Coal India Ltd.
during the first quarter of current financial
year;
(b) the production done by these
subsidiary units as against the target;
(c) if the production is below the target,
the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps being taken to improve
the production?
 Signing of pact between MCL and
NALCO
†1218. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Orissa based Mahanadi
Coalfields Ltd. (MCL) has signed any pact
to give coal to nearby National Aluminium
Company Ltd. (NALCO);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it has become a practice to
give coal to companies of distant States
instead of power plants of other industries
situated in those States, where subsidiary
companies of Coal India are situated; and
(d) if not, the factual position obtaining
in the matter?
 Extension of broadband coverage to
schools
1219. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have formed
an Inter-Ministerial Group comprising of
various Ministries such as Health, Home,
Human Resource Development, Panchayati
Raj and IT to discuss for planning the
rollout of broadband infrastructure and
indicate their requirement in rural areas with
support from the Universal Services
Obligation Fund;
(b) whether Government have set up a
target of adding 6.5 million broadband
subscribers in 2007, of which 4.5 million
are expected to be provided by BSNL; and
(c) whether Government are also
planning to extend broadband coverage to
all secondary and higher secondary schools
by 2007 and public healthcare centres
by 2010?
 Closure of post offices
1220. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that post offices
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

281
have been closed in several parts of the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the number of employees who have
been affected; and
(d) the reasons for such closure?
 Broadband services in the country
1221. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had set a target
of 9 million Broadband connections by 2007
and 20 million by 2010;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are satisfied
with the pace of development in this field
keeping in view the present growth rate;
and
(d) if not, the steps which are being
taken to increase the penetration of
Broadband services in the country?
 Third Generation Wireless
Communication services
1222. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had received
any recommendations from TRAI regarding
3rd Generation Wireless Communication
Services in September, 2006;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) by when the licences are expected to
be awarded and to how many operators;
(d) whether Government are considering
to allow foreign operators for 3 G services
and if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to
accommodate one of its Public Sector
Undertakings therein;
(f) the other players who are likely to
be accommodated therein; and
(g) by when the process of licensing is
likely to be completed?
 IT Park in Gulbarga
1223. SHRI K.B. SHANAPPA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to start
an IT park in Gulbarga (Karnataka);
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Waiving of roaming charges
1224. SHRI RAJ NATH SINGH: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the residents of Greater Noida, Gurgaon
and Noida areas are paying huge amount of
the roaming charges on the BSNL Mobile
(Cell One);
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

282
(c) whether Government have any plan
to waive off roaming charges in these areas?
 Revision of NFAP
1225. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Frequency Allocation Plan (NFAP) is
revised every two years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that draft
NFAP has been prepared in 2005 and that
all the stakeholders did not agree to this
draft, document; and
(c) if so, the reasons for Government to
come out with draft NFAP-2007 before
the spectrum policy and ITU-R frequency
allocation recommendations?
 Committee on Information,
Communication and
Entertainment
1226. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: W ill the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have set up
any Committee on Information,
Communication and Entertainment to help
players in these sectors grow to their full
potential;
(b) if so, the composition thereof;
(c) whether the Committee has
submitted its report; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon?
 Facilities for village postmen
†1227. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that village
postmen are provided the facilities of salary,
allowance, LTC and pension;
(b) if not, the reasons for denial of these
common facilities despite serving in remote
areas in such hard conditions;
(c) by when the facilities like salary,
allowance and pension etc. would be
allowed to them like other postal
employees;
(d) whether it is a fact that for months
together they have not been getting any
salary; and
(e) if so, the reasons therefor?
 Procurement of GSM handsets by
BSNL
1228. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to issue a fresh tender for the procurement
of GSM handsets by BSNL;
(b) if so, the reasons for the disposal of
existing tender;
(c) the amount of loss incurred and loss
of consumer base to BSNL in terms of delay
in procuring the GSM handsets; and
(d) the reasons for the delay in
procuring the handsets despite the
completion of tendering process?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

283
 Unique software package for
e-governance
1229. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to develop a unique software package for
its much acclaimed e-governance;
(b) if so, the progress achieved towards
that end;
(c) whether Government are considering
to incorporate spreading free software
developers in development of software
packages;
(d) if so, the steps taken in this regard;
and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Electronic telephone exchanges
1230. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of electronic telephone
exchanges set up in the country particularly
in the State of Assam, during the last three
years, State-wise/District-wise/year-wise;
(b) the details of such telephone
exchanges proposed to be set up in Assam
during this period, location-wise; and
(c) the details of financial grants
allocated by Government for this purpose,
State-wise?
 Reduction of FDI for ISPs
1231. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that TRAI
recommended for reducing the FDI in
Internet Service Providers from the existing
limit of 100 per cent to 74 per cent;
(b) if so, the details of the
recommendation;
(c) whether this recommendation has
been made by TRAI in view of poor record
of Internet Service Providers;
(d) whether it is also a fact that out of
700 licences issued in the last three years,
not even half exist today and only 135
internet service licenses are functionally
active; and
(e) if so, how his Ministry are planning
to go ahead in this sector?
 Delay in procuring equipments
1232. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of subscribers which
BSNL adds each month;
(b) the reasons for having no additions
in the month of April, May and June 2007;
(c) whether it is a fact that the company
has already lost Rs. 110 crore in revenue
because of the delay in procuring
equipments; and
(d) if so, by when the equipments would
be procured?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

284
 Recovery of bills through
intimidation
†1233. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that TRAI has
received complaints wherein it has been
stated that means like threatening and
intimidation are being resorted to by
different mobile companies for recovery of
bills;
(b) if so, the number of such complaints
